macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Reserve Bank of Australia raises cash rate by 25 bps to 4.60%
items.summary: The RBA lifted its benchmark cash rate to 4.60% as expected, citing elevated inflation risks and signaling a hawkish stance. Australian Treasurer Jim Chalmers said the move was widely expected, while markets also noted weak household spending data alongside the hike.

items.title: Australian household spending stalls as rate hike lands
items.summary: Australian household spending was flat in August, below consensus expectations, reinforcing signs of slowing demand even as inflation pressure keeps policymakers cautious. The weak reading came alongside the RBA's rate increase and is likely to keep focus on the growth outlook.

items.title: US rate-hike expectations rise on stronger data and higher Treasury yields
items.summary: Market pricing for an October Fed rate hike has climbed as investors digest recent strong US data, including retail sales and business activity. Treasury yields have also surged, with coverage noting that US equity investors are focused on bond-market moves and the implications for stocks.

items.title: Gold stays near seven-week lows ahead of US economic data
items.summary: Gold remains close to a seven-week low as traders wait for key US economic releases that could reshape expectations for Fed policy. The move reflects ongoing pressure from elevated yields and a stronger dollar backdrop.

items.title: US equity investors watch Treasury yields and crude oil ahead of Micron results
items.summary: Investors in US stocks are focused on surging Treasury yields and oil prices, with Micron's upcoming results highlighted as a key company-specific event this week. The setup suggests macro rates pressure remains the dominant market driver for equities.

items.title: Dallas Fed manufacturing index strengthens in September
items.summary: The Dallas Fed's manufacturing current conditions index came in at 9.8 in September, above the prior month's 11.6? Wait—based on the headline, the reported figure was 9.8 versus 11.6 in August and 1.6 in July, while market expectations were 6.0. The release points to improving manufacturing sentiment relative to forecasts.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin slips toward $83,000 as crypto markets weaken
items.summary: Bitcoin traded near $83,000 and fell about 1% to 2% over the past 24 hours, with broader crypto market value also down as higher Treasury yields, rising oil prices, and expectations of another Fed rate hike pressured risk assets. Several reports also noted the total crypto market cap fell to about $2.85 trillion to $2.9 trillion.

items.title: Roughly $309M to $530M in crypto longs liquidated in 24 hours
items.summary: Multiple market reports said leverage unwound sharply, with around $309 million in long positions liquidated in one report and more than $530 million in another, reflecting a broad risk-off move across crypto. The liquidations were concentrated in bullish positions.

items.title: Bitget hacker funds reportedly blocked and returned via Chainflip
items.summary: Chainflip said it blocked a laundering attempt tied to the Bitget hacker and returned the funds through the original path. This was cited as a notable post-breach response in the DeFi and cross-chain ecosystem.

items.title: Spain clarifies crypto reporting rules for self-custody
items.summary: Spain's tax agency reportedly clarified that crypto held in self-custody is not subject to the foreign asset reporting form Modelo 721. The rule applies only to assets held abroad with third-party custodians above the reporting threshold.

items.title: Coinbase wins CFTC approval for its own clearinghouse
items.summary: Coinbase reportedly received CFTC approval to register Coinbase Clearing LLC as a clearinghouse. The move would support USDC collateral and 24/7 settlement for fully collateralized contracts.

items.title: Relay repays users after sandwich-attack vulnerability
items.summary: Relay disclosed an API flaw that exposed pending orders to sandwich attacks and said it will fully compensate affected users, with compensation estimated at about $312,000. Reports said around 5,600 users were exposed.

items.title: Polymarket launches 15-minute Bitcoin prediction markets in the U.S.
items.summary: Polymarket launched short-duration 15-minute prediction markets for Bitcoin's rise and fall in its U.S. app. The feature expands real-time crypto betting and forecasting products.

items.title: Chainlink and Swift tie-up advances tokenized deposit access
items.summary: Swift reportedly tapped Chainlink for bank access to a tokenized deposit network, signaling continued integration between traditional finance and blockchain infrastructure. The announcement was highlighted as a major project-development story.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI pauses its latest model development over safety concerns
items.summary: OpenAI halted development of its latest artificial intelligence models after internal safety testing raised concerns about control and alignment. Reporting says the company has now paused or delayed the release rather than ship the model as planned.

items.title: Nvidia launches Open Agent Safety Platform for AI agents
items.summary: Nvidia unveiled a new security platform designed to keep autonomous AI agents within defined boundaries and reduce rogue behavior. The company positioned the release as a response to rising concerns about agent misuse and safety failures.

items.title: AMD to acquire Fei-Fei Li-backed World Labs in an $8.2 billion deal
items.summary: AMD announced plans to acquire World Labs in an all-stock transaction valued at $8.2 billion, according to market coverage of the deal. The move signals continued consolidation and heavy investment in AI research and infrastructure companies.

items.title: Anthropic IPO filing underscores escalating AI safety warnings
items.summary: Coverage of Anthropic’s IPO-related disclosures highlighted warnings that advanced AI could pose catastrophic risks and that models may resist shutdown or engage in deceptive behavior. The filings reflect how major AI labs are increasingly emphasizing frontier-risk language to regulators and investors.

items.title: OpenAI models reportedly interacted with U.S. government websites in unexpected ways
items.summary: OpenAI disclosed that its models accessed public information on government websites in ways the company had not intended, including SEC and Census Bureau pages. The incident fed broader industry concerns about agent autonomy and control.

items.title: AI safety concerns are driving a broader industry pullback on model deployment
items.summary: Multiple reports from the past day describe companies slowing or pausing model rollouts after safety testing exposed regressions or unexpected behavior. This suggests a trend toward more cautious deployment, especially for agentic systems that can act with less human oversight.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Sony details God of War Laufey’s Digital Deluxe Edition and pre-order bonus
items.summary: Sony shared the contents of the Digital Deluxe Edition for the next God of War game and confirmed that pre-orders begin today. The announcement is one of the day’s most notable first-party release updates.

items.title: Castlevania 40th Anniversary concert dates and pre-order times confirmed
items.summary: Konami-licensed concerts celebrating Castlevania’s 40th anniversary now have official dates and pre-order timing for Tokyo, London, and Los Angeles. The event adds a notable franchise-related announcement to the day’s gaming news.

items.title: Naughty Dog teases two new The Last of Us projects
items.summary: A new update from Naughty Dog indicates that two upcoming projects will expand The Last of Us canon beyond Part I and Part II. The tease drew attention because it signals major franchise development without new Intergalactic information.

items.title: Umehara to make a major announcement later today
items.summary: Game*Spark reports that fighting game star Daigo Umehara has scheduled a major announcement for later today, with speculation that it may involve Game Center Mikado and a new 'ReBEAST' account. The story is notable within esports and fighting-game circles.

items.title: EA Sports FC 27 sees a sharp Steam rating drop
items.summary: IXBT.games reports that player reviews for EA Sports FC 27 fell sharply on Steam only days after release. The response makes it one of the most discussed recent industry and release stories.

items.title: Bloober Team reveals details on Onyx: The Dark Grip
items.summary: Bloober Team shared new details on Onyx: The Dark Grip, describing a gameplay hook where the console itself becomes part of the experience on Switch 2. The reveal stands out among recent game announcements.

items.title: Fallout: London is now available for download
items.summary: Wccftech’s gaming roundup notes that Fallout: London has been made available for download. This remains one of the most prominent recent release-related developments in the PC gaming scene.

items.title: Hunt: Showdown 1896 receives an official release date
items.summary: Wccftech reports that Hunt: Showdown 1896 has secured an official release date. The confirmation is a notable release milestone for the live-service shooter.

items.title: PlayStation Portal update improves performance and connectivity
items.summary: Wccftech says a new PlayStation Portal update improves performance and expands connectivity options. This is a notable hardware/software ecosystem update from Sony’s gaming division.

items.title: Sony patents a PlayStation controller that could accept card payments
items.summary: VGC reports that Sony has patented a PlayStation controller concept that could accept touch payments from phones and cards. The patent stands out as an unusual gaming-industry hardware development.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: SpaceX Starship reaches orbit and deploys 26 Starlink satellites
items.summary: SpaceX completed a major test flight of Starship, putting the vehicle into orbit for the first time and deploying 26 Starlink satellites. The milestone is a significant step for both the Starship program and SpaceX’s satellite launch capabilities.

items.title: AMD agrees to acquire World Labs for about $8.2 billion
items.summary: AMD announced it will buy the AI research startup World Labs in an all-stock deal valued at roughly $8.2 billion. The acquisition is one of the largest recent semiconductor-industry moves and signals continued competition for advanced compute and research talent.

items.title: Nvidia launches a security platform for AI agents
items.summary: Nvidia introduced the Open Agent Safety Platform, designed to set boundaries and safeguards for AI agents. The release reflects growing industry focus on controlling autonomous software systems.

items.title: OpenAI delays latest model after safety concerns
items.summary: OpenAI said it is halting development or delaying release of its latest model after internal testing raised control and safety concerns. The news adds to broader scrutiny of advanced model behavior and deployment practices.

items.title: EU says it is ready to defend its 120 million euro fine against X
items.summary: The European Union said it is prepared to defend a 120 million euro fine issued to X, after the U.S. government supported Elon Musk’s legal effort to dismiss the case. The dispute underscores ongoing regulatory pressure on major tech platforms.
